findings.where: Article specimen, the PDF entry 'Streamlining the PPP Process' under the blog post's last paragraph (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The one PDF entry has no heading. It sits in the article's own column, straight after the post's closing line, between two rules. By proximity and by the shared column it reads as an attachment or a 'related' link of this blog post, not as the start of Mark's list of articles and talks. The brief calls that list the product.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader who finishes the post can't tell whether this is the post as a PDF or a separate lecture. The founder, judging the PDF list as the depth after the first look, sees no list at all, only one unlabelled row.

findings.where: First screen, the 'Placeholder: Mark's photo…' caption: bottom left at 1440, and on phone after the action, about 500 px below the photo
findings.fault: The caption sits with the text column, under the action, far from the photograph it describes. On the desktop the photo is on the right half and the caption on the left; on the phone the caption sits after the button. Proximity groups it with the action, not the image.
findings.who_objects: The founder judging the first screen has to work out what the note refers to. A reader on the phone may take it as small print about the email address.

findings.fault: The footer puts the mark and wordmark first on the left. Mark's name sits about 600 px away on the far right, run together with the address. The header has the name leading with the logo beside it; the footer breaks that pairing, so the logo leads and the name is detached.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose personal-advisor test asks that his name leads with the logo beside it. The page's two lockups disagree with each other.

findings.where: Left edge, first screen against every section below it (hero and nav at about 58 px; palette, type pair, texture, article, motion and footer at about 170 px)
findings.fault: The hero's text and nav hang from one left edge, and the whole page below, footer included, steps in to a second edge about 110 px further right. Continuity breaks at the fold: the footer, a site component, doesn't line up with the header it pairs with.
findings.who_objects: The founder or Angélique, who would build the site from this tile. They wouldn't know which edge is the site's margin, and on the real homepage the header and footer would visibly fail to line up.

findings.where: Phone, the palette's text-pair table (top of phone-02)
findings.fault: At 390 px the three columns squeeze the ratio cell, so '11.66 : 1' breaks into '11.66 :' and a stray '1' on the next line. The swatch labels ('warm white on slate') also wrap under their chips.
findings.who_objects: Anyone checking the palette on a phone reads a broken figure. A specimen that can't set its own values cleanly undercuts the 'refined' claim.

findings.where: Type pair specimen, the Newsreader and Public Sans columns (desktop-02 into desktop-03)
findings.fault: The two face names share a line, but the descriptions under them don't share a top edge. Public Sans's paragraph starts about 30 px higher than Newsreader's because its sample name is smaller, so the paired columns look slipped against each other.
findings.who_objects: The founder comparing the pair side by side: a small misalignment in the one section about typographic care.
